name: Metrocare Services – Samuell Adult Mental Health Clinic
services: Adult outpatient mental health clinic providing psychiatric evaluation, medication management, counseling, and case management.
population: Adults with mental health needs in Dallas County, including serious mental illness.
eligibility: Primarily serves Dallas County residents; accepts Medicaid and public funding; options for uninsured through county programs.
intake: Call clinic or Metrocare intake line for screening and appointment; referrals accepted from hospitals and providers.
hours: Weekday business hours; see website for current schedule.
cost: Publicly funded safety-net care; most services low or no cost for eligible clients.
notes: Local Mental Health Authority (LMHA) for Dallas County; one of Metrocare’s main adult clinics.

name: MHMR of Tarrant County – Behavioral Health Services
services: Community mental health center offering psychiatric care, individual and group therapy, substance use treatment, and 24/7 crisis services.
population: Children, adolescents, and adults in Tarrant County with mental health or substance use needs.
eligibility: Primarily serves Tarrant County residents; accepts Medicaid and other public funding; uninsured may qualify for county-funded services.
intake: Call the MHMR intake line or 24/7 crisis line for screening and referral to outpatient services.
hours: Office open weekdays; crisis line and some crisis services available 24/7.
cost: Publicly funded care; low/no cost for eligible individuals.
notes: Local Mental Health Authority for Tarrant County; key access point for county-funded therapy and psychiatry.

name: LifePath Systems – Behavioral Health Services (Plano)
services: Outpatient mental health services including psychiatric evaluation, medication management, counseling, and crisis services.
population: Adults, children, and families in Collin County with mental health needs.
eligibility: Primarily serves Collin County residents; accepts Medicaid and some other insurance; county funding for eligible uninsured/low-income clients.
intake: Call main number for screening and to schedule an intake; referrals accepted from hospitals, schools, and community agencies.
hours: Weekday business hours; some programs may offer extended hours – see website.
cost: Public mental health provider; many services low/no cost depending on funding and eligibility.
notes: LifePath is the Local Mental Health Authority for Collin County and provides safety-net behavioral health care.

name: Jewish Family Service of Greater Dallas – Counseling Services
services: Individual, couples, and family counseling; psychiatric services; support groups; specialized programs for trauma, grief, and family relationships.
population: Children, teens, and adults of all backgrounds (services are non-sectarian).
eligibility: Serves anyone regardless of religion; accepts some insurance and offers sliding-scale fees based on income.
intake: Call main number to complete intake and be matched with a therapist or psychiatrist.
hours: Weekday office hours; some evening appointments available – see website.
cost: Nonprofit counseling center with sliding-scale and reduced-fee options; some grant-funded services may be low-cost or free.
notes: Well-established nonprofit providing culturally sensitive counseling, case management, and psychiatric care.

name: Child & Family Guidance Center – Dallas
services: Trauma-informed counseling, psychiatric evaluation and medication management, play therapy, family therapy, and integrated behavioral health.
population: Children, adolescents, and adults with emphasis on underserved families and trauma survivors.
eligibility: Serves North Texas residents; accepts Medicaid/CHIP and many commercial plans; offers sliding-scale or reduced fees for eligible low-income/uninsured clients.
intake: Call intake line to complete screening for child, teen, or adult services and schedule an appointment.
hours: Weekday clinic hours; some evening availability depending on location and program.
cost: Community mental health center and Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC); many services available at reduced cost.
notes: Strong focus on childhood trauma, family systems, and long-term outpatient counseling and psychiatry.

name: UT Southwestern – Multispecialty Psychiatry Clinic (Adult)
address: 6363 Forest Park Rd, 8th Floor, Dallas, TX 75390
services: Academic medical center clinic providing psychiatric evaluation, medication management, and psychotherapy for mood, anxiety, psychotic, and other disorders.
population: Adults needing specialty psychiatry or combined medication and psychotherapy in the DFW area.
eligibility: Accepts many commercial insurance plans, Medicare, and some managed Medicaid products; self-pay and financial assistance options through UT Southwestern.
intake: Call clinic to request a new patient appointment; referrals from primary care or other providers often helpful for triage.
hours: Weekday daytime hours; some clinicians may offer limited evening hours – see website.
cost: Hospital-based specialty clinic; standard medical billing with UT Southwestern financial assistance options.
notes: Good fit for complex or treatment-resistant conditions that may benefit from academic medical center expertise.

name: UT Southwestern – Center for Depression Research and Clinical Care (CDRC)
services: Specialized evaluation and treatment programs for depression, bipolar disorder, and related mood disorders; integrates evidence-based psychotherapy, medication, and research opportunities.
population: Adolescents and adults with moderate to severe depression, bipolar disorder, or treatment-resistant mood disorders.
eligibility: Patients typically need to meet diagnostic criteria for mood disorders; insurance coverage varies by clinic program; some services associated with research studies may have different costs/requirements.
intake: Call CDRC to inquire about current clinical programs and research options and to complete a screening call.
hours: Weekday clinic hours; schedule varies by program and research study.
cost: Standard academic medical center billing for clinical services; some research participation may reduce cost for specific interventions.
notes: Highly specialized mood-disorders program; good option for complex depression/bipolar cases and those interested in research-based care.

name: Dallas CBT
address: 3500 Oak Lawn Ave, Suite 230, Dallas, TX 75219
services: Outpatient therapy and assessment clinic specializing in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), exposure therapies, EMDR, and psychological testing for ADHD and related concerns.
population: Children, teens, adults, and couples seeking evidence-based treatment for anxiety, OCD, trauma, depression, and related issues.
eligibility: Primarily serves private-pay and insured clients in DFW; accepts some insurance plans and provides documentation for out-of-network reimbursement.
intake: Call office or use website contact form to request an appointment and therapist match.
hours: Typical office hours Mon–Fri with some evening appointments by arrangement – see website.
cost: Private group practice; session-based fees; check website or call for insurance and out-of-network details.
notes: Strong CBT/EMDR focus; good fit for anxiety, OCD, trauma, and clients wanting structured, skills-based therapy.

name: The Center for Integrative Counseling and Psychology
services: Individual, couples, and family counseling; psychological testing; school-based and church-based counseling through partnerships; workshops and support groups.
population: Children, teens, adults, and older adults across DFW, including underserved communities reached via satellite sites.
eligibility: Nonprofit; accepts many insurance plans and employee assistance programs (EAPs); also offers reduced-fee counseling through sliding scale and community partnerships.
intake: Call central office or use online form; clients are matched with a counselor at the main office or a partner site (schools, churches, community centers).
hours: Weekday business hours; some evening and off-site hours depending on counselor and location.
cost: Sliding-scale and low-cost options available; mission is to make counseling accessible regardless of ability to pay.
notes: Multi-site nonprofit counseling center serving Dallas, Collin, Tarrant, and surrounding counties with a large therapist network.

name: Dallas Therapy Collective
address: 8140 Walnut Hill Ln, Suite 440, Dallas, TX 75231
services: Group practice providing trauma-informed individual and couples therapy with specializations in LGBTQ+-affirming care, gender-affirming care, EMDR, religious trauma, anxiety, and depression.
population: Teens (13+) and adults, with particular focus on LGBTQ+ clients, trauma survivors, and people with marginalized identities.
eligibility: Private practice; accepts some insurance (varies by therapist) and self-pay; some clinicians offer superbills for out-of-network reimbursement.
intake: Use website to contact a specific therapist or submit a general inquiry; phone number available for scheduling assistance.
hours: Weekday office hours; many clinicians offer evening or telehealth appointments – see individual therapist pages.
cost: Private group practice; fees vary by clinician; some offer limited sliding-scale spots.
notes: Progressive, intersectional, LGBTQ+-affirming practice; strong fit for clients seeking trauma-informed and identity-affirming care.

name: The Counseling Place
services: Affordable professional counseling; trauma and crime-victim counseling; youth and prevention programs.
population: Adults, teens, children, families, crime victims
eligibility: Open to the general public; grant-funded no-cost counseling available for victims of crime and police referrals (Richardson and Sachse).
intake: Call main number or use website contact form to request an appointment; no walk-ins.
hours: Mon–Thu 9:00am–5:00pm; Fri 9:00am–1:00pm; Sat–Sun closed.
cost: Sliding-scale and low-cost services; no-cost counseling for eligible crime victims; most programs supported by grants and donations.
notes: Nonprofit mental health agency serving Richardson since 1979; offers in-person and telehealth counseling.

name: Richland Oaks Counseling Center
services: Individual, couples, and family counseling; psychological assessment; trauma, anxiety, depression, relationships; reduced-fee training clinic with graduate interns.
population: Children, teens, adults, couples, families
eligibility: Open to the public; sliding-scale reduced fees available, especially with graduate student clinicians.
intake: Call office or email to request an appointment; all services by appointment only.
hours: By appointment only; daytime and evening availability varies by clinician.
cost: Sliding-scale options (including lower-cost sessions with interns); standard private-pay rates vary by clinician; some insurance accepted.
notes: Training and community counseling center; multiple licensed psychologists and interns under supervision.

name: Meltzer Counseling PLLC
services: Evidence-based psychotherapy (ACT, CBT, DBT skills); mood and anxiety disorders; trauma and PTSD; addiction; relationship and family therapy; some family programs offering no-cost sessions for qualifying families.
population: Teens, young adults, adults, couples, families
eligibility: Open to the public; Family Tree Program provides free family counseling for eligible families in Dallas/Denton County (subject to funding and criteria).
intake: Call office or submit the online contact form to be matched with a clinician; telehealth and in-person options.
hours: Mon–Fri 8:00am–9:00pm; weekends and evenings by appointment.
cost: Accepts many commercial insurance plans; private-pay available; limited no-cost or reduced-fee family services through specific grant programs.
notes: Group practice with diverse clinicians and specialties; offers both in-person and HIPAA-compliant telehealth sessions.

name: Love Roots Therapy PLLC
address: 100 N Central Expressway, Suite 310, Richardson, TX 75080
services: Individual and couples counseling; trauma and attachment-focused therapy; anxiety, depression, self-esteem and life transitions; LGBTQIA+ affirming care.
population: Young adults, adults, couples, LGBTQIA+ community
eligibility: Open to adults and couples; affirming of diverse identities and relationships; some telehealth availability for Texas residents.
intake: Request an appointment via online client portal or call office; brief consultation often available before scheduling.
hours: By appointment only; hours vary by therapist.
cost: Primarily private-pay; some clinicians may accept insurance or provide superbills for out-of-network reimbursement; fees and sliding-scale options vary by provider.
notes: Small, relationship-focused practice emphasizing authenticity, inclusivity, and trauma-informed care.

name: Linden Tree Counseling PLLC
address: 1755 N Collins Blvd, Suite 310, Richardson, TX 75080
services: Child and play therapy; anxiety and ADHD treatment; parenting support; individual and family counseling; faith-integrated counseling available by request.
population: Children, teens, adults, parents, families
eligibility: Open to the public; some clinicians paneled with insurance plans; telehealth offered for older teens and adults.
intake: Call office or use online contact form to request an intake; all visits scheduled in advance.
hours: By appointment; daytime and after-school/evening slots depending on clinician.
cost: Standard sessions around $135; accepts some insurance plans and HSA/FSA; exact rate and coverage depend on provider and plan.
notes: Offers child-friendly play therapy rooms and family-systems-oriented treatment for anxiety, behavior, and adjustment issues.

name: Journeys Christian Counseling Center
address: 100 N Central Expy, Suite 614, Richardson, TX 75080
services: Christian-based counseling for individuals, couples, and families; marriage and relationship counseling; anxiety, depression, grief, life transitions and spiritual issues.
population: Adults, couples, families, some teens
eligibility: Open to the public; services provided from a Christian worldview but generally available to anyone comfortable with faith-integrated counseling.
intake: Call main number or use website contact form to be scheduled with a counselor; appointments required.
hours: By appointment; hours vary by counselor, with some evening availability.
cost: Primarily private-pay; some clinicians may accept insurance or offer sliding-scale fees; clients should verify costs when scheduling.
notes: Long-standing Christian counseling center (established in the early 1990s) serving the North Dallas/Richardson area.

name: Richardson Christian Counseling (Texas Christian Counseling – Richardson)
address: 100 N Central Expressway, Suite 532, Richardson, TX 75080
services: Faith-integrated individual therapy; couples and family counseling; treatment for anxiety, depression, trauma and PTSD, grief, codependency, relational and family issues; online counseling available.
population: Children, teens, adults, couples, families
eligibility: Open to the public; Christian-oriented care for clients who want to include faith; most counselors are licensed mental health professionals and many accept insurance.
intake: Call reception line or submit a contact form to be matched with a counselor and schedule an intake.
hours: By appointment; hours depend on individual counselor, including some evenings and weekends.
cost: Many providers accept commercial insurance; private-pay and some reduced-fee options may be available; verify benefits prior to first visit.
notes: Association of licensed Christian counselors serving Richardson and surrounding North Dallas suburbs in person and via telehealth.

name: New Directions Counseling and Wellness Center
address: 1901 N Central Expressway, Suite 220, Richardson, TX 75080
services: Individual counseling; couples, marriage, and family therapy; anxiety and depression treatment; grief and loss; adolescent and parenting counseling; neurofeedback services.
population: Adolescents, adults, couples, families
eligibility: Open to the general public; some clinicians specialize in family and couples work; telehealth available for many services.
intake: Call office or use website contact form to schedule; some clinicians allow direct email or extension-based scheduling.
hours: By appointment; daytime and some evening hours depending on provider.
cost: Private-pay practice; some clinicians accept insurance or provide superbills for out-of-network reimbursement; fees vary by therapist and service type.
notes: Multi-clinician practice offering both traditional talk therapy and neurofeedback; provides crisis hotline information on site for suicidal emergencies.

name: Jeremy R. Cooper
services: https://www.jeremycooperlpc.com
population: Specialized therapy for PTSD and complex trauma; dissociative disorders; grief and loss; anxiety; Christian counseling upon request; research-informed, depth-oriented psychotherapy.
eligibility: Adults (including trauma survivors, clients with chronic illness, and faith-oriented clients)
intake: Open to adult clients; in-person sessions in Richardson and HIPAA-compliant telehealth for Texas residents; accepts some commercial insurance (including Aetna).
hours: Request an appointment via website contact form or call main number; all sessions by appointment only.
capacity: By appointment only; scheduling tailored individually (daytime and some evening options).
cost: Unknown
contact_email: Accepts Aetna and some other insurance plans; private-pay rates available on request; out-of-network benefits may apply for other plans.
notes: Jeremy.Cooper@richlandoaks.org
column15: Solo practice located inside Richland Oaks Counseling Center; integrates research, philosophy, and spirituality for trauma-informed care.

name: Texas Health Behavioral Health Center – Richardson
address: 3661 N Plano Road, Suite 2100, Richardson, TX 75082
services: Hospital-affiliated behavioral health center offering mental health assessments; outpatient therapy and psychiatric services; adult and adolescent behavioral health programs; coordination with higher levels of care (PHP/IOP/inpatient) in the Texas Health system.
population: Adults and adolescents needing structured outpatient or step-down behavioral health care
eligibility: Open to the public; may require insurance or self-pay and clinical appropriateness for specific programs; typically serves North Texas residents.
intake: Call clinic directly or Texas Health behavioral health intake line for screening and appointment scheduling; referrals may also come from providers or hospitals.
hours: Hours of operation vary by program; generally weekday hours with some extended programming—call for current schedule.
cost: Accepts most major insurance plans and Medicare/Medicaid where applicable; hospital billing with self-pay and financial assistance options per Texas Health policies.
notes: Outpatient behavioral health hub at Texas Health CityLine; useful for higher-acuity clients who need psychiatry, structured programs, or hospital system support.
